primitives.name: Material Composition
primitives.verbatim_quote: THE MATERIAL If the material at the start is to be without defect there must be the following: r.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M': 'team material vector, dimensionless', 'R_i': 'role i requirement, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Team composition is modeled as a finite-dimensional vector space over role requirements.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \(\exists i : M_i < R_i \), team is deficient.

layer2.mapping: Vector space projection of team roles onto idealized role basis; GSI computes posterior probability of victory given \(M\).
layer2.telemetry: Player role fulfillment metrics and substitution availability.

primitives.name: Player Role Sufficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: Unless the material has players capable of fulfilling these requisites, and good substitutes to take their place, the material is weak.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_j': 'substitute j availability, binary', 'P_k': 'player k capability, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Each role requires a player with sufficient capability and a substitute.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \(\forall k: P_k < threshold \vee \neg S_j\), team is weak.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between player capability vector and role fulfillment tensor; GSE evaluates state transitions via role coverage.
layer2.telemetry: Role-specific player performance and substitution readiness.

primitives.name: Coach Adjustment Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the ordinary case there are generally one or two weaknesses in the material which must be adjusted by skillful coaching.
primitives.assumptions: Coaching efficacy is a function of observed weakness count and skill level.

layer2.mapping: State transition map from material deficiency to tactical correction; GSI models coaching impact via Bayesian feedback.
layer2.telemetry: Tactical adjustments made and outcome variance.
